Package neqsim.process.safety.selfheating

Class SelfHeatingInductionSolver

java.lang.Object
neqsim.process.safety.selfheating.SelfHeatingInductionSolver
public class SelfHeatingInductionSolver extends Object
Transient one-dimensional solver for the induction time (time to ignition) of a self-heating body.

PorousMediaSelfHeatingAnalyzer answers whether a body will ignite. This solver answers when, by integrating the transient conduction equation with an Arrhenius volumetric source

rho * c * dT/dt = lambda * (d2T/dr2 + (j / r) * dT/dr) + P * exp(-E / (R * T))

where j is 0 for a slab, 1 for a cylinder and 2 for a sphere. The timing matters operationally: lagging fires characteristically smoulder for hours or days before breaking out, so a leak that stopped long ago can still ignite, and the absence of an immediate fire after a spill is not evidence of safety.

The body starts at a uniform initial temperature and its outer surface is held at the boundary temperature (Dirichlet). Symmetry is imposed at the centre. Integration uses explicit Euler with a time step limited by both the conduction stability criterion and the local reaction time scale, so the step shrinks automatically as the reaction accelerates.

A run terminates when the peak temperature exceeds the boundary temperature by the ignition rise (default 100 K), or when the profile becomes steady, or when the maximum simulated time is reached.
